{{short description|German mathematician}}
{{for|the botanist|Hans Fitting (botanist)}}

'''Hans Fitting''' (13 November 1906 in München-Gladbach (now [[Mönchengladbach]]) – 15 June 1938 in [[Königsberg]] (now [[Kaliningrad]]))
was a mathematician who worked in [[group theory]]. He proved [[Fitting's theorem]] and [[Fitting's lemma]], and defined the [[Fitting subgroup]]
in [[finite group theory]] and the [[Fitting decomposition]] for [[Lie algebra]]s and [[Fitting ideal]]s in [[ring theory]].

After finishing his [[undergraduate]] work in 1931, he wrote his [[dissertation]] with the help of [[Emmy Noether]], who helped him secure a [[Grant (money)|grant]] from the ''Notgemeinschaft der Deutschen Wissenschaften'' (Emergency Society for German Sciences). He died at the age of 31 from a sudden bone disease.<ref>[[Auguste Dick|Dick, Auguste]]. ''Emmy Noether: 1882–1935''. Trans. H. I. Blocher. Boston: Birkhäuser, 1981. {{ISBN|3-7643-3019-8}}. pp. 54–55.</ref>
